nodes.label: norn (worktree + agent-session TUI)
nodes.rationale: Named for the Norns weaving threads of fate at the world tree: worktrees are the threads, git is the tree. Tagline "many threads, one tree".

nodes.label: One worktree per task
nodes.rationale: Isolated checkout per task removes stashing and branch-juggling when switching between parallel pieces of work.

nodes.label: Single tabbed TUI program
nodes.rationale: One process with Tab / 1-4 switching replaces separate commands, so context stays in one place; ? shows keys, esc backs out, q quits.

nodes.label: Threads tab (worktree dashboard)
nodes.rationale: Live view across repos of branch, PR state and age; enter cd's in, o opens the agent, / filters, m jumps to the main checkout.

nodes.label: New tab (create worktree from hint)
nodes.rationale: Hint becomes a Conventional Branch name; T seeds from a real tracker task, M picks the model.

nodes.label: Clean tab (prune merged/gone worktrees)
nodes.rationale: Auto-selects worktrees whose work is merged or whose remote branch is gone so pruning is one keystroke rather than an audit.

nodes.label: Settings tab (in-place config editing)
nodes.rationale: Edits agent, template, theme and toggles with a global/project layer switch, writing YAML surgically so comments and hand-added keys survive.

nodes.label: shell-init cd integration
nodes.rationale: A child process cannot change its parent shell's directory, so a shell wrapper is eval'd from the binary itself; shipping it inside the binary means it never drifts from the implementation. Optional, norn degrades to not moving the shell.

nodes.label: norn review <pr#>
nodes.rationale: Checks the PR branch out into a worktree so the agent reviews real code it can read, run and comment on, fork PRs included, rather than a text diff.

nodes.label: norn diff viewer
nodes.rationale: For a quick read without spending a worktree: uncommitted changes, branch-vs-base, or any open PR, with split view and syntax highlighting.

nodes.label: --since-review comment overlay
nodes.rationale: Overlays your own review comments, including outdated ones, next to the current code so comment and fix are readable in one scroll.

nodes.label: Local agent review to .norn/review.md
nodes.rationale: Reviewing the agent should not require a PR or a public repo. R writes comments grouped by file, anchored path:line, blocking count at the top, then resumes the agent pointed at it so one pass replaces a dozen round-trips. .norn/ belongs in .gitignore because the review is yours, not part of the change.

nodes.label: Conventional-comment labels in review
nodes.rationale: Each comment gets a conventionalcomments.org label with one key (i/s/n/q/t/p/h/o) plus b for blocking, so intent is explicit and cheap to type.

nodes.label: Configurable coding agent (agent.command)
nodes.rationale: Claude Code is the default but any CLI agent works: with claude the brief is injected via --append-system-prompt and resumed with -c; other agents are launched in the worktree where .worktree.md carries the brief. Thread summaries and AI branch naming are Claude-only and simply do not run otherwise.

nodes.label: .worktree.md brief templates
nodes.rationale: Ships task and review; user files in ~/.config/work/templates/<name>.md.tmpl shadow a built-in so customization never forks the binary.

nodes.label: Tracker task seeding (github | clickup)
nodes.rationale: norn only seeds branch name and hint from a tracker task; the agent's own MCP does the deep work, so norn deliberately is not an MCP client. github reuses existing gh auth so no token is needed.

nodes.label: Theme system (nord, frog)
nodes.rationale: nord is arctic frost + aurora, frog is mossy greens with a dashboard avatar; a palette is a few lines in internal/tui/styles.go, kept cheap on purpose to invite PRs.

nodes.label: Zero-config with layered overrides
nodes.rationale: Works with no config at all; norn init scaffolds a per-project file, global defaults live in ~/.config/work/config.yaml, and --project-config / doctor make the resolved state inspectable.

nodes.label: Graceful degradation of optional tooling
nodes.rationale: Only git is required. gh unlocks PR features and claude launches sessions, but both are optional so a missing tool disables a feature instead of breaking the program.
